references.text: Earlier in the chapter, the Israelites are commanded to eat unleavened bread together with the Passover lamb, which establishes the basis for the seven-day Feast of Unleavened Bread.
Repeats the prohibition against leaven and the consequence of being cut off from the congregation of Israel, extending it to apply to both foreigners and native-born.
Confirms the command to eat unleavened bread for seven days and that no leaven shall be found in the land.
The Feast of Unleavened Bread is mentioned as one of the three annual feasts, with the command to eat unleavened bread for seven days.
Repeats the command regarding the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days in the month of Abib.
Detailed regulations for the Feast of Unleavened Bread, including the seven days and holy assemblies.
Confirms that the feast lasts seven days during which unleavened bread is to be eaten.
The command to eat unleavened bread for seven days is repeated, called 'bread of affliction' as a reminder of the exodus from Egypt.
Six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a holy assembly.
Paul uses the symbolism of leaven and unleavened bread to explain that believers should cleanse out the old leaven and live in purity and truth, with Christ as our Passover lamb.
Extends the prohibition from individual houses to the entire land to emphasize total purity.
Explains the theological basis for unleavened bread as a memorial of the exodus from Egypt.
Specifies the offering rules for the first day and confirms the prohibition against leaven.
Sets the start date for the seven days of unleavened bread following Passover.
Prophetic restoration of the Passover feast in the future temple.
